A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. The changed title, formatting and appendix organization do not prevent reliable matching.

before.justification: Sections 3–5 and the appendices report original analyses of coding accuracy, resampling rewards, code readability and failure cases, alongside theoretical-model simulations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and simulations. Results retained from v1 remain original results of this work.

M1.justification: The resampling procedure, unit-test verification and generator–verifier setup are unchanged. The new discussion of reasoning-model training introduces an application hypothesis, not a new implemented method.

E1.justification: The documented experiments retain HumanEval+/MBPP+ correctness and readability tasks. However, new Appendix E mentions a HotPotQA analysis using Llama models without corresponding methods or results anywhere in v3. Whether question-answering coverage was actually added is therefore unresolved.

E2.justification: Figures 3–7 and the corresponding appendix plots retain the same model membership within each comparison. Removing reasoning, critique and fusion from Table 1 changes the literature survey, not the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: v3's main-text specification of 200 HumanEval+ samples, 1,000 for Command Light, and 50 MBPP+ samples matches details already in v1 Appendix A.2.1. Temperature, task exclusions, reward settings and readability evaluation procedures are retained; no experimental increase is established.

E4.justification: The cost-benefit sensitivity, task-difficulty analyses, low-precision-verifier subset analysis and qualitative failure cases are retained. The HumanEval/30 demonstration moves from v1 Figure 8 to v3 Figure 18; it is not a new case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 random permutations of fixed samples for reward estimation and retain the same regression statistics and missing-solution bounds. Adding 'worst-case' to v3 Figure 12 clarifies bounds already reported in v1 Figure 13.

E6.justification: The matched plots retain their results, including Figure 3's R-squared values of 0.891 and 0.892 for HumanEval+ and MBPP+. Reward curves, optimal-sample heatmaps, readability scores and failure findings also match. The altered Figure 4 panel only removes an axis label.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix A.3 and v3 Appendix C retain the same two-difficulty model, assumptions, parameter values and Equations 1–6 for rejection probabilities, posterior beliefs and expected rewards. Emphasizing domain-independent applicability adds no formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The principal claims about resampling ceilings, optimal sample counts and code quality remain. The abstract, introduction and discussion extend the implications to rejection-sampled training data and a potential bottleneck for competitive reasoning models, beyond v1's more general warning about verifier-related training risks.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges that deployment-specific cost-benefit ratios lack empirical validation and that larger sampling budgets may remain practical in lower-stakes settings. It also develops the mislabeled-training-data interpretation, explicitly presents the reasoning-model bottleneck as a hypothesis, and emphasizes the theory's domain-independent applicability.

D1.justification: New Appendix E discloses OpenAI/Azure endpoint use and states that no local GPU inference or model training was required, although its HotPotQA statement is unsupported elsewhere. Notebook access changes from a direct Colab link to a named supplementary file. The repository and generated-sample release were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds reasoning-model references including DeepSeek-R1, Sky-T1 and Bespoke-Stratos, and distinguishes its setting from Gao et al.'s reward overoptimization work. It prunes reasoning/critique/fusion limitations and test-generation references, and revises its criticism of prior resampling work. The APPS citation now incorrectly resolves to the MMLU paper.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten and parts of the discussion expanded, while the main Sections 1–6 retain their organization and much of their wording. Reproducibility moves into the main text; appendices are reorganized, resource and impact statements are added, and citations switch to author–year style.

P2.justification: The document receives extensive template, typography and layout changes, with resized and relocated displays. Table 1 contracts from seven technique rows to four; Figure 1 moves off the opening page; the main-text code demonstration moves to the appendix. Reformatted Figures 23, 29 and 30 restore previously truncated modulo expressions.

improvement.justification: The explicit cost-ratio limitation in Section 6 and repaired code listings make the existing evidence easier to interpret and inspect. These are modest gains, since the experiments and theory remain unchanged. The benefit is tempered by conjectural training implications, the unsupported HotPotQA mention and the new APPS/MMLU citation mismatch.
